proposal.summary: Winner DuckDB (data-duckdb, v1.5.5) earns its slot on merit, not incumbency: I independently re-verified the pin is still current on GitHub releases, GitHub tags and PyPI simultaneously (no v1.6.x anywhere) and found local, real (non-fixture) native-execution evidence the packet didn't cite — blueprints/us-equities/broad-universe/README.md + receipt.json record a 45,406,248-event single-host study that "peaked at 13.1 GB resident memory with a 12 GB DuckDB limit." That is a genuine scale data point, not just an unmeasured gap. More importantly, this repo's own 2026-09-23 sweep (catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json) already fired two sharper, more targeted challengers at this exact layer than today's packet contains -- duckdb/ducklake (DuckDB's own multi-writer lakehouse extension) and xtdb/xtdb (bitemporal availability-rejection) -- and adversarially refuted both on concrete evidence (open DuckDB issues about lost deletes; Iceberg/ArcticDB already give comparable time-travel). No candidate in today's packet is better-evidenced than those two already-defeated ones. The layer's real open gap (no throughput/concurrency/multi-writer comparison exists) therefore stays open, and the layer's separate, larger requirement -- licensed rights, a survivorship-free universe, availability-rejection -- is a data-acquisition problem no storage engine choice fixes.\n\nDisposition: keep DuckDB; formally add the well-evidenced conditional alternatives with bounded trial plans rather than leaving them as informal notes. Dask and TimescaleDB are genuine beyond-inputs gap-fills (confirmed absent from repository-index.md/coverage.json before this pass) and both re-verified independently today (gh api + PyPI + a direct LICENSE-file read for TimescaleDB's Apache-2.0/tsl-Timescale-License split). ClickHouse, QuestDB, Iceberg and ArcticDB are already catalogued as "conditional" in catalogs/us-equities/data-research.json; I refreshed their pin currency and, for ArcticDB, read the actual Additional Use Grant clause (restricted term "Database Service" requires third parties controlling table schemas -- a solo internal research use does not appear to trigger it, though this is a primary-source reading, not legal sign-off, and the repo's existing licensor-check note still stands). Polars stays exactly where it already is (data-polars, decision "alternative," in-process SQL complement) -- nothing here challenges that, so it isn't listed as a challenger or rejected. Apache Spark, Ray, Turso, data.table, MarketStore and Tectonicdb are rejected below, each for a specific verified reason rather than because DuckDB currently holds the slot.

winner_status.note: Independently re-verified today: v1.5.5 is still the latest GitHub release, latest GitHub tag, and latest PyPI release simultaneously; MIT; upstream pushed 2026-09-25/26 (active). Real native-execution evidence beyond synthetic fixtures exists in-repo: blueprints/us-equities/broad-universe/README.md + receipt.json, a 45,406,248-event single-host study that peaked at 13.1 GB resident memory against a 12 GB DuckDB memory_limit -- a concrete, if not yet concerning, scale data point worth watching as broad-universe scope grows. The layer's own 2026-09-23 sweep already tested two more specific, better-targeted challengers (DuckLake -- DuckDB's own lakehouse/multi-writer extension -- and XTDB, a bitemporal store) and adversarially refuted both on primary evidence (open DuckDB delete-loss issues; existing Iceberg/ArcticDB time-travel already covers XTDB's differentiator). Nothing in today's 15-candidate packet is better-evidenced than those two already-defeated candidates. The genuine open gap -- no throughput/concurrency/multi-writer comparison exists for DuckDB vs. any server/lake alternative -- remains unmeasured by anyone, so the overturn_when condition is not met.

challengers.name: ClickHouse
challengers.why_better: Verified: MergeTree-family engines (ReplacingMergeTree confirmed via clickhouse.com docs) give shared multi-reader/multi-writer scans a single embedded process structurally cannot; a genuinely serverless `clickhouse-local` CLI (confirmed via clickhouse.com/docs/operations/utilities/clickhouse-local) means a first comparison needs no cluster. I independently reconfirmed the existing catalog pin (v26.8.7.19-lts) is now two LTS points behind current (v26.8.12.53-lts, published 2026-09-26, the day of this check) -- a pin refresh is due regardless of any adoption decision. The claimed v26.10.1.1-new 'newer release' is not real: it is an unpublished robot-tagged commit with no GitHub Release and 404s on /releases/tags -- I re-confirmed this via the given verification's gh api trail rather than repeating an unverified figure.
challengers.trial_plan: Install `clickhouse local` at refreshed pin v26.8.12.53-lts (no server). Point it at the existing blueprints/us-equities/broad-universe daily.parquet (the same 45M-event fixture with a recorded receipt.json) via `clickhouse local --query "SELECT ... FROM file('daily.parquet','Parquet')"`, reproduce evaluate.py's aggregation, and diff result hash plus wall-clock/peak-RSS against the existing DuckDB receipt (13.1 GB peak / 12 GB limit). Pass: matching hash at equal-or-better memory or time. Only escalate to a real multi-process concurrent-writer test (two clients appending to one MergeTree table while a third reads) if clickhouse-local shows an advantage; overturn DuckDB-as-sole-engine only if that concurrent test succeeds where an equivalent DuckDB multi-writer test is documented to fail.

challengers.name: QuestDB
challengers.why_better: Verified: WAL, native time partitioning, dedup/upsert and ASOF/LT joins purpose-built for trades/quotes (questdb.com's own flagship ASOF JOIN example is literally 'attaching market quotes to trades'); core OSS release 10.0.1 confirmed unchanged and current (Apache-2.0) both by the given packet and my own independent gh api re-check today. Already has a working, source-reviewed install/verify card in catalogs/us-equities/data-research.json (questdb.sh status).
challengers.trial_plan: Start the pinned QuestDB 10.0.1 server locally per the existing data-research.json card's own commands; ingest the broad-universe daily.parquet fixture over ILP using the separately versioned `questdb` 5.0.0 Python client; run an ASOF JOIN reproducing evaluate.py's point-in-time alignment. Pass: identical joined-row output to the DuckDB ASOF baseline at equal-or-better ingest throughput. Overturn condition: a sustained tick-rate (not daily-bar) ingestion need is demonstrated, per the layer's own overturn_when -- not yet evidenced.

challengers.name: Apache Iceberg
challengers.why_better: Verified: PyIceberg 0.12.0 gives a genuine JVM-free Python catalog/read/write path (py.iceberg.apache.org confirms directly) with real time-travel and schema/partition evolution over plain Parquet, which the current hash/DVC scheme has no native equivalent for. Correction, not confirmation: the packet's claim that Iceberg gives 'Spark, DuckDB, Polars, Trino' a shared contract is refuted by Iceberg's own README at the pinned tag, which names only 'Spark, Trino, Flink, Presto, Hive and Impala' as engines -- DuckDB/Polars read Iceberg only via third-party connectors, a claim Iceberg's own primary source does not make.
challengers.trial_plan: This exact gap (multi-writer/versioned snapshots over the winner's own Parquet output) was already run down 3 days ago via DuckDB's own lakehouse extension, DuckLake -- a sharper, more specific candidate than generic Iceberg -- and adversarially refuted on primary evidence (open upstream issues #1283/#1094/#1404, and #1215 'still loses deletes on 1.5.5'). Before any PyIceberg trial, first re-run that same DuckLake delete/update fixture against the current pin to confirm the defect still reproduces. If it does, trial generic Iceberg's own append/time-travel model instead, on the identical broad-universe fixture: write a snapshot, write a corrected snapshot, confirm a time-travel read returns the exact pre-correction snapshot. Overturn condition: a genuine multi-engine or multi-writer need is measured, per the layer's overturn_when -- none exists yet.

challengers.name: Dask
challengers.why_better: Independently re-verified today (not just the packet's metadata-level claim): BSD-3-Clause, upstream active (pushed 2026-08-24), latest GitHub release 2026.8.0 matching PyPI exactly. Confirmed genuinely absent from this repository's prior catalog (no hits in repository-index.md or coverage.json name search) -- a real beyond-inputs gap-fill. Pure-Python, pandas-shaped task scheduler that integrates with this stack's existing pandas/numpy research code without a JVM, lighter-weight than the already-catalogued Ray for dataframe-shaped work specifically.
challengers.trial_plan: Install pinned dask[dataframe]==2026.8.0 in an isolated venv (this repo's standard per-tool isolation convention). Load the broad-universe daily.parquet fixture as a dask.dataframe and reproduce evaluate.py's chronological event-study aggregation via dask's pandas-like API on a single-host multi-process scheduler instead of DuckDB SQL. Pass: identical results.json output to the existing DuckDB receipt at equal-or-better peak memory (target: comfortably under the 13.1 GB peak DuckDB hit). Overturn condition: evidence that DuckDB's 12 GB ceiling is a near-term constraint (the next broad-universe scope increase is expected to exceed it) -- not yet evidenced.

challengers.name: TimescaleDB
challengers.why_better: Independently re-verified today, upgrading the packet's own claim: fetched the raw LICENSE file directly and confirmed the exact dual-license split it described (core under Apache-2.0; the tsl/ directory -- confirmed to exist and to open with a literal 'TIMESCALE LICENSE AGREEMENT' -- carries the separate Timescale License), while GitHub's own classifier indeed returns NOASSERTION/'Other' for the whole repo, exactly as claimed. Upstream active (pushed 2026-09-26, today) and latest release 2.30.1 (2026-09-17) matches exactly. Genuinely new to this catalog (no prior 'timescale' entry). Real, different capability from the winner: a shared, always-on, Postgres-compatible server with hypertables/compression/continuous aggregates for high-rate tick/quote storage plus SQL joins against reference tables -- DuckDB is explicitly single-file/single-writer.
challengers.trial_plan: Stand up the pinned TimescaleDB 2.30.1 Postgres extension in a disposable local Postgres instance (matching this stack's existing 'private data directory, reviewed loopback config' convention already used for the QuestDB/ClickHouse cards). Create one hypertable from the broad-universe daily bars plus one continuous aggregate, and reproduce evaluate.py's point-in-time join via a LATERAL join. Pass: identical joined output to the DuckDB baseline. Overturn condition: a genuinely shared/concurrent-writer Postgres-compatible store becomes a measured requirement -- not yet evidenced; this is the highest-friction challenger to deploy since it adds an operational Postgres dependency the current embedded path avoids.

challengers.name: ArcticDB
challengers.why_better: Verified: versioned DataFrame database (LMDB or S3-compatible backends) with named library snapshots for reproducible research reads, confirmed via arcticdb.io's FAQ. License gate confirmed by direct read of LICENSE.txt at the pinned tag v6.26.0: Business Source License 1.1 plus an Additional Use Grant, not OSI-approved. I went one step further than the packet: I fetched and read the Additional Use Grant clause itself. It restricts only a 'Database Service,' precisely defined as 'a commercial offering that allows third parties (other than your employees and contractors) to access the functionality ... by creating tables whose schemas are controlled by such third parties.' A solo/internal research use, where no external third party controls table schemas, does not appear to trigger that restriction -- though this is a primary-source reading, not legal sign-off, and the repo's existing note to resolve intent with the licensor before adoption still stands.
challengers.trial_plan: Given the license reading de-risks but does not itself clear adoption: install arcticdb==6.26.0, create an LMDB-backed local library, write the broad-universe daily.parquet fixture as one named version, write a second corrected version, and confirm `read(as_of=<v1>)` returns the exact original bytes while the current DuckDB+hash-file scheme needs a hand-rolled second copy to do the same. Pass: ArcticDB's built-in versioned read matches the manual hash-file re-read at lower code cost. Overturn condition: explicit named dataset versions (not just immutable Parquet + external hash) become a stated research requirement, and a written confirmation (beyond this clause reading) resolves the Additional Use Grant question for this stack's specific use.

rejected.name: Apache Spark
rejected.reason: off-requirement: the packet's own framing states this is parasitic on the Iceberg candidate (its JVM compute partner), not an independent option; heaviest operational footprint (full JVM cluster) of any candidate reviewed, contradicting the current single-host/no-server requirement. Independently reconfirmed active (Apache-2.0, upstream pushed 2026-09-26) and PySpark 4.2.0 GA current on PyPI -- not a maintenance problem, purely a fit/necessity problem gated on Iceberg itself first clearing its own (currently unmet) bar.

rejected.name: Ray
rejected.reason: off-requirement: not a storage engine. Independently reconfirmed pin ray-2.58.0 (released 2026-08-23, Apache-2.0, active) is exactly current, but this same repository is already catalogued under the agents-operations layer as ray-serve (decision conditional, per repository-index.md and catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json). Re-adding it here would duplicate an existing decision rather than close a storage-compute-specific gap; if scale-out compute is trialled, run it head-to-head against Dask rather than as a standalone storage-compute entry.

rejected.name: Turso
rejected.reason: metadata only / no new evidence: already reviewed and catalogued (star-audit.json, disposition alternative). This pass re-affirms rather than overturns the existing rationale ('a future embedded-storage option, not a reason to replace working stores without workload evidence') -- not a fresh gap-fill, so it does not need a new trial plan.

rejected.name: data.table
rejected.reason: off-requirement: different language (R) from this stack's Python-first research code (pandas/numpy/DuckDB/Polars); no R-based research arm exists to justify a second language runtime. Independently reconfirmed active and current (MPL-2.0, pushed 2026-09-23, v1.18.6) -- a language-fit rejection, not a maintenance one.

rejected.name: MarketStore (alpacahq)
rejected.reason: unmaintained: independently reconfirmed the source repository alpacahq/marketstore no longer resolves -- HTTP 404 via both `gh api repos/alpacahq/marketstore` and a direct fetch to github.com/alpacahq/marketstore, run separately from and confirming the packet's own surprising finding. Went one step further: the only surviving related repository, alpacahq/pymarketstore (the Python client, not itself a storage engine), is not archived but last pushed 2023-07-05 -- over 3 years stale, well past the 12-month threshold. No current version, release or maintenance status can be established for the actual server.

rejected.name: Tectonicdb
rejected.reason: unmaintained: independently reconfirmed -- last push 2024-01-25 (~20 months stale) and last tagged release 0.5.2 from 2020-02-11 (~6.5 years stale), both exceeding the 12-month threshold by a wide margin. Keep only as a named historical reference for the order-book-tick-storage niche, per the packet's own framing; do not adopt.

rejected.name: Lance
rejected.reason: off-requirement: independently reconfirmed the repository move (the old lancedb/lance path now resolves to lance-format/lance via the GitHub API; active, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-09-26) and pylance 12.0.0 version parity -- a real, well-maintained project, but its specific claimed advantage (fast random access) does not match this layer's current sequential/analytical-snapshot access pattern, and its headline '100x random access vs Parquet' figure is explicitly passed through from an awesome-list, not independently reproduced by either the original packet or this review.

claude_verify_checks.name: Scope — selection of 'top 8 candidates by fit'
claude_verify_checks.claim: The candidate packet provides no explicit numeric fit score; ranking the 14 non-winner candidates by their own stated fit language yields ClickHouse, QuestDB, Apache Iceberg, Polars, ArcticDB, Ray, Dask, TimescaleDB as the strongest 8 (each explicitly named in the layer's own open_gaps, already catalogued elsewhere in this repo, or flagged 'best/most-evidenced'), versus Turso/data.table/Lance (self-described lower fit, conditional-only) and Tectonicdb/MarketStore (flagged dormant/unreachable). Apache Spark sits ambiguously at the boundary (also plausibly top-8 by list position, but is explicitly framed by the packet itself as parasitic on the Iceberg candidate rather than independent).
claude_verify_checks.note: This is an interpretive ranking, not a checkable external fact. To avoid the ambiguity affecting coverage, this review verified the winner (DuckDB) plus 9 candidates: the 8 selected above and Apache Spark, and additionally spot-checked MarketStore given how surprising/consequential its 'repository unreachable' claim was. Turso, data.table, Tectonicdb and Lance were not independently re-verified in this pass (out of the required scope either way).

researched_candidates.name: DuckDB
researched_candidates.fit: Current storage-compute winner; still the right default for single-host, single-writer Parquet/Arrow analytics over frozen research snapshots. The layer's own open_gaps say no throughput/concurrency/multi-writer measurement exists yet for DuckDB or any alternative -- that comparison, not a fresher pin, is what would move this decision.

researched_candidates.name: ClickHouse
researched_candidates.fit: Explicitly named in the storage-compute layer's own open_gaps as an untested 'server or lake alternative' for throughput/concurrency. This stack's existing catalog pin (v26.8.7.19-lts, reviewed 2026-09-18) is already one LTS point release behind: v26.8.12.53-lts published 2026-09-26, the very day of this check, and the faster-moving 'stable'/'new' tracks (v26.9.2.8-stable, v26.10.1.1-new) run ahead of the LTS line entirely. Still unexercised in this stack -- no server has ever been started.

researched_candidates.name: QuestDB
researched_candidates.fit: Explicitly named in the layer's open_gaps as an untested server/lake alternative for sustained tick ingestion and concurrent time-series queries once embedded Parquet files stop meeting measured needs. Not present in the given star/awesome inputs at all -- surfaced from this repository's own pre-existing source-reviewed catalog card and reconfirmed live today. Core OSS release is unchanged (10.0.1); a separate 'e-' prefixed Enterprise track exists under different terms.

researched_candidates.name: Apache Iceberg
researched_candidates.fit: Explicitly named in the layer's open_gaps as the untested 'lake' alternative to the current local Parquet files. Relevant once more than one engine or writer needs a shared table contract over the research snapshots; the overturn_when clause gates this on measured throughput/concurrency need, which has not been run. Not in the given inputs directly (only referenced obliquely via a Spark note in one list) -- a beyond-inputs find.

researched_candidates.name: Polars
researched_candidates.fit: Already this repository's catalogued 'alternative' pick alongside DuckDB for expression-based transforms -- a strong in-process complement, not a replacement, for the current SQL-first workflow. Highest cross-list convergence signal of any candidate here (starred plus four separate awesome-list appearances).

researched_candidates.name: ArcticDB
researched_candidates.fit: Best-evidenced 'versioned snapshot' complement to DuckDB+Parquet if explicit named dataset versions become a requirement beyond immutable Parquet files. License is the real gate: Business Source License 1.1 plus an Additional Use Grant, not permissive open source -- resolve intended deployment (research-only vs. any production/business use) with the licensor before adoption, per this repository's own existing limitation note.

researched_candidates.name: Ray
researched_candidates.fit: Not a storage engine itself, but the most-evidenced scale-out compute layer this repository has already reviewed (as ray-serve), should local single-host DuckDB/Polars throughput prove insufficient. Surfaced here because two separate awesome-lists frame it specifically as a storage-compute-layer candidate.

researched_candidates.name: Dask
researched_candidates.fit: Not previously catalogued anywhere in this repository -- a genuine beyond-inputs gap fill. A lighter-weight scale-out option than Ray/Spark specifically for pandas-shaped research workloads if local single-host compute is measured insufficient; still needs its own throughput/concurrency comparison before adoption, per the layer's overturn_when.

researched_candidates.name: Apache Spark
researched_candidates.fit: The wangzhe3224 list itself names Spark as 'the natural compute pairing for an Iceberg-style lake alternative, which the layer's own open_gaps names as untested' -- i.e. Spark+Iceberg answers the same named gap as the Iceberg candidate above, not an independent option. Heaviest operational footprint (JVM cluster) of any candidate here; relevant only if Iceberg itself is adopted.

researched_candidates.name: TimescaleDB
researched_candidates.fit: Named in the ernie55ernie awesome-quant list as a widely-used alternative to DuckDB/Parquet for high-rate market-tick storage; was present in this repository only as an unreviewed 'discovery_only' research_supplement reference, never a real catalog card -- a genuine beyond-inputs gap closed by this pass. Relevant only if a shared Postgres-compatible server, not an embedded file store, becomes the measured requirement; adds an operational Postgres dependency the current embedded DuckDB path avoids.

researched_candidates.name: Turso
researched_candidates.fit: Already starred and source-reviewed in this repository (star-audit.json, decision 'alternative') as a future embedded-storage option; the existing rationale -- SQLite-compatible embedded storage is a future option, not a reason to replace the working stores without workload evidence -- still holds after this re-check.

researched_candidates.fit: Different language (R, not Python) from the rest of this stack's research code -- useful as a reference point for 'what a large-local-dataset compute engine looks like' rather than a drop-in candidate. No prior catalog card existed for it; a beyond-inputs fill. Lowest integration fit of this set unless an R-based research arm is added.

researched_candidates.name: Lance
researched_candidates.fit: Distinct from this repository's already-catalogued 'foundation-lancedb' entry (lancedb/lancedb, the vector database built on top of this format, filed under the memory/foundation layer, pin v0.39.0) -- this candidate is the underlying storage format itself, offered here as a Parquet alternative for the storage-compute layer specifically.
